open_points.subject: create_expense_from_recognition orchestration requirement
open_points.text: create_expense_from_recognition: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST accept only confirmed complete normalized input whose contract_version equals the version of a row of the imported SUPPORTED_OCR_CONTRACT_VERSIONS constant, validate explicit allocations, apply R8 replay before mutation, and atomically insert one Expense plus one ExpenseDocument plus allocations and the expense.create member of = models.AuditAction audit.
open_points.question: Must the note name the declared EXPENSE_CREATE member, or must the AuditAction enum expose a member named expense.create?

open_points.subject: create_expense_from_recognition audit requirement
open_points.text: create_expense_from_recognition: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST build exactly one audit intent with the imported build_project_audit_intent from the context, the expense.create member of = models.AuditAction as action, the EXPENSE member of = models.AuditEntityKind as entity_kind and the expense_id of the expense of the inserted aggregate as entity_id, and append it via the audit repository PortalTransaction.audit returns, then commit exactly once and return the outcome the imported build_expense_operation_outcome builds from the inserted aggregate.
open_points.question: Must the note name the declared EXPENSE_CREATE member, or must the AuditAction enum expose a member named expense.create?

open_points.subject: create_expense_from_recognition publication completeness requirement
open_points.text: create_expense_from_recognition: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise ExpenseValidationError, before it projects the publication and before any transaction or write, when the received publication object lacks a field that = models.ConfirmedRecognitionPublication declares, such as confirmed_at on an instance built bypassing validation; the check MUST test that every declared field is set on the received instance and MUST NOT rely on catching a generic attribute error.

open_points.question: Must the prompt permit a declared field-set/introspection surface for checking all fields, or must the requirement be changed to validation achievable solely through the listed fields?

open_points.subject: _validate_initial_allocations dependency requirement
open_points.text: _validate_initial_allocations: [DEPENDENCY_BOUNDARY] MUST raise FinancialValidationError for an instruction whose target is the SECTION member of = models.AllocationTargetKind without section_id, one whose target is its other_expenses member carrying a section_id, any other target, and an allocation total that differs from the total_amount of the intake, all before opening any transaction; it MUST then open exactly one transaction, resolve every SECTION target only by calling get_project_section of the project_sections repository PortalTransaction.project_sections returns with the project_id of the intake and the section_id, and close that read transaction by exactly one PortalTransaction.rollback, marking it closed before it raises ExpenseValidationError for a missing or cross-project section so that rejection keeps the 422 status the legacy BudgetValidationError produced; it MUST NOT call validate_project_section, a PortalStore lookup, or a legacy PortalTransaction project-section method.

open_points.text: create_expense_from_recognition: [RETURN_SHAPE] When the expenses repository PortalTransaction.expenses returns returns an existing aggregate for the recognized_document_id, MUST close that read transaction by exactly one PortalTransaction.rollback, marking it closed before _classify_expense_replay evaluates the fingerprint, then return its ExpenseOperationOutcome with replayed true for an equal fingerprint or raise ExpenseConflictError unchanged; neither replay path may append an audit or mutate storage.
